Written by George Harrison , it was the only non Lennon – McCartney song on the Sgt Pepper album. The song was Harrison’s second full-blown Indian recording, after Revolver ’s ‘Love You To’ . Although regarded by some as a dull interlude in the otherwise masterful Sgt Pepper , ‘Within You Without You’ encapsulated the exploration of spiritual themes that had become popular in 1967’s Summer of Love. Clear references to the counterculture (‘Are you one of them?’) and the LSD-related ego death (‘And to see you’re really only very small and life flows on within you and without you’) can be found amid the more other-worldly exploration of spiritual philosophy and religious teachings.
